title: [dagster-postgres] use pg_notify() so bound payload works under psycopg3
body:
## Summary & Motivation

Fixes #34232.

`PostgresEventLogStorage.store_event` issues `NOTIFY run_events, :notify_id` with the payload as a bound parameter. NOTIFY is a utility statement and does not take bind parameters, so under psycopg3 (SQLAlchemy 2.1's default postgres driver) this renders as `NOTIFY run_events, $1` and Postgres rejects it. Every event write fails.

This switches the call to `SELECT pg_notify('run_events', :notify_id)`. pg_notify is a regular SQL function, so the payload stays bound and compiles cleanly under both pyformat and numeric_dollar paramstyles.

## Test Plan

No live postgres on this machine, so I verified the compiled SQL with SQLAlchemy 2.1.1 directly:

- pyformat (psycopg2): `SELECT pg_notify('run_events', %(notify_id)s)`
- numeric_dollar (psycopg3): `SELECT pg_notify('run_events', $1)`

Both valid. Before the fix, numeric_dollar rendered `NOTIFY run_events, $1`, which Postgres rejects. I did not run the dagster-postgres test suite (needs a live postgres).

## Changelog

Fixed `dagster-postgres` event log writes failing under psycopg3 by sending the notification payload through `pg_notify()` instead of a bound `NOTIFY` command.

title: [dagster-postgres] use pg_notify for bound event notifications
body:
Refs #34232

## Summary

```PostgreSQL
NOTIFY run_events, :notify_id
```

is currently issued through SQLAlchemy with a bound payload. Under psycopg3 / SQLAlchemy's server-side bind style, that becomes `NOTIFY run_events, $1`, which PostgreSQL rejects because `NOTIFY` is a utility statement and does not accept a bind placeholder there.

This changes the notification to PostgreSQL's `pg_notify(channel, payload)` function instead. Because it is a regular SQL function, the channel and payload can remain safely bound and compile correctly for both client-side and server-side parameter styles.

## Changes

- use `SELECT pg_notify(:channel_name, :notify_id)` in `PostgresEventLogStorage.store_event`
- keep both the channel and notification payload as bound parameters
- add regression coverage that compiles the production statement with SQLAlchemy's `numeric_dollar` parameter style and asserts `SELECT pg_notify($1, $2)`

## Validation

Validated the production statement with SQLAlchemy locally:

- PostgreSQL pyformat style: `SELECT pg_notify(%(channel_name)s, %(notify_id)s)`
- server-side numeric-dollar style: `SELECT pg_notify($1, $2)`

I have not run the full Dagster test suite locally.

## Scope

This PR addresses the `NOTIFY ... $1` failure from #34232. It deliberately does not change Dagster's PostgreSQL driver packaging/default-driver policy; first-class psycopg3 packaging is already being discussed in #33958.

title: [dg api] Filtered `run get-events` no longer skips events when paging with its cursor
body:
## Summary & Motivation

With `--level`, `--event-type` or `--step`, `dg api run get-events` filters events on the client. `DgApiRunEventApi._fetch_with_filters` pages through the run's events and keeps the matching ones. Every page asked the server for `limit` events, so a single page could hold more matches than were still needed. The extra matches were cut off by `events[:limit]`, but the returned `cursor` was the page's end cursor, which is already past them. When you continue with `--cursor <that cursor>` (as the output suggests: "use --limit to increase or --cursor to paginate"), those events are never returned.

Example: `--level INFO --limit 3` on the events `[INFO 1, DEBUG, DEBUG, INFO 2, INFO 3, INFO 4, INFO 5]`. The first page (3 events) has 1 match. The second page (3 more events) has 3 matches, so it returns 1, 2 and 3 and drops 4. The cursor points after event 6, so the next call returns only `INFO 5`. `INFO 4` is never shown.

This fix keeps pages at the full `limit` size, so sparse filters search just as far as before. When the limit is reached partway through a page, the fix re-reads that one page from its start cursor, asking only for events up to the last one kept (`limit=i + 1`). The cursor it returns then points right after the last event returned. This costs one extra request, and only when a page overflows.

## Test Plan

- Added `test_filter_cursor_does_not_skip_matching_events`. It uses a mocked `get_run_events` that honors `limit` and returns the index of the next event as its cursor. The test fetches `--level INFO --limit 3`, then fetches again with the returned cursor, and asserts that the two calls together return all 5 matching events. On `master` it fails: `assert ['match-5'] == ['match-4', 'match-5']`.
- Added `test_sparse_filter_keeps_full_page_size`: 200 events with matches at 0 and 150 and `limit=2`. Both matches are found and the cursor is exactly `151`. This covers the page-cap concern from review.
- Updated `test_filter_paginates_until_limit_then_truncates`. It asserted that the cursor was `cur-2`, the end of the overflowing page, which is the value that skips the dropped event. It now expects the re-read of page 2 from `cur-1` with `limit=1` and that re-read's cursor.
- With the fix, `pytest dagster_rest_resources_tests/` passes (349 tests), and so does `pytest dagster_dg_cli_tests/cli_tests/api_tests/run_tests` (44 tests, 30 snapshots).
- `ruff check` and `ruff format --check` (ruff 0.16.2) pass on the changed files.

This PR was found and written by an AI coding agent (Claude), opened from the breken-ai account.

## Changelog

> `dg api run get-events` with `--level`, `--event-type` or `--step` no longer skips matching events when you page through results with `--cursor`.
